validated_work_order.approach:
Two files. One declaration in the stylesheet, and one abstraction in the test file that every stylesheet pin in it then uses — so that at the end of this change there is no second CSS parser left in the suite. Plus the one-line repair that makes the suite green so any of it can be verified. Three repairs to v6 are folded in and marked R1-R3 below; they are corrections to the ORDER, not to the diagnosis or the design.

R1 — THE QA BOOT IS FIXED SO THE BROWSER HALF MEASURES SOMETHING. The scratch DB_PATH prefix goes on BOTH commands, and step 1 gains a non-vacuity assertion before any measurement is taken: after seeding and serving, `GET /journal?state=partial` must contain `class="awaiting-list"` and a decision id of the seeded length, and the echo must show ONE seeded database rather than a 4096-byte schema-only file. This is not a convenience. As v6 wrote it, the seed wrote ./data/app.db and the server read an empty scratch file, so every `scrollWidth == clientWidth` check in AC-2 and AC-10 passed on a page with no awaiting list at all — and posting a valid decision did not help, because the API does not create a tenant row, `firstTenant()` returned null and `decisionsOf` returned []. I reproduced exactly that. The assertion is the difference between a browser acceptance and a vacuous one, and it costs one curl.

R2 — THE RENDER HALF'S FIXTURE IS SPECIFIED IN FULL. `repos.decisions.create(...)` binds nine values into nine NOT NULL columns; a two-field call throws `TypeError: Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 3` before the test runs. The full shape is: `{ tenant_id: 'tenant_demo', decision_id: <140 unbreakable chars>, state_snapshot_id: 'state_pin', action_class: 'budget-change', selected_action: 'raise_budget', decided_at: <ISO>, expected_evaluation_at: <ISO>, status: 'awaiting-maturity' }`. I ran this exact shape on `seededRepos()` and it returns `created: true`. The supporting claim is corrected rather than repeated: the repository performs no validation of its own, and the table's NOT NULL columns are what make a partial row a TypeError from node:sqlite — which is why the shape is named in full rather than described.

R3 — THE ch-only NARROWING IS A NAMED EDIT WITH ONE NAMED EXCEPTION TO 'VERBATIM'. The min-width floor regex narrows from /^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(ch|rem|px)$/ to ch-only, and its one failure message changes from 'floors the field at a readable width in ch, rem or px' to name ch. That is the ONLY assertion or message in this change that is not preserved verbatim, and it is named here so files[] and AC-6 stop contradicting AC-5. It is a strictness decision, not a verified defect: `min-width: 96px` is a value a legitimate edit could reach for, and it goes red for no semantic reason beyond 'not ch'. That cost is recorded in risks and in out_of_scope so a maintainer can overrule it deliberately. tests[]'s self-contradiction about 96px is resolved: 96px goes RED.

A. Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere;` to the EXISTING `.awaiting-list li` rule in src/web/styles.css, in place among its display / gap / border / border-radius / padding declarations, with one comment in the same voice and for the same reason as the wrap rule at styles.css:385-393: a grid item is floored at its min-content width, the decision_id is free text, `anywhere` rather than `break-word` because break-word creates the break opportunity but leaves intrinsic sizing alone. NOT as a second rule with the same selector — the new pin's conflict check would read the fix as an override of itself.

B. Add four shared helpers near the top of test/web/pages.test.js, beside H1_HOOK (line 23) and mainOf (line 37), and route all eight stylesheet read sites through them. Only the plumbing moves, with the single R3 exception.

  `readStylesheet()` — the single readFileSync of src/web/styles.css, returning the SOURCE STRING. Every one of the eight sites becomes `const css = readStylesheet();` — the shape they have today — and the parse is one call on top. It returns the string rather than the parsed rules on purpose: the card pin's and the tenant pin's `length > 0` guards and failure messages are about the file, and the forced-colors pin's source-order assertion is easiest to read against the text it is ordering. This also makes AC-9's grep mean exactly what it says.

  `cssRules(source)` — strip /* */, then walk with a brace stack. A frame whose selector starts with '@' is a BLOCK whose children are rules; any other frame is a rule whose body is declarations. ';' terminates a declaration inside a rule and a prelude inside an at-rule. Nested rules are emitted with their own selector and a nested flag meaning 'not at top level'. At-rule frames are not emitted. Every rule carries a source index. TWO FAILURE MODES PRODUCE PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT AND NEITHER SHOWS UP UNTIL A PIN DEPENDS ON IT: accumulating the prelude through a rule body concatenates `width: 100vw;` onto the selector of the next nested rule, and a reader that appends nested text to the parent body instead of descending into it drops every nested rule and reinstates the at-rule blind spot exactly — while passing every test in the file as written today. This order pins NO magic rule count: a total breaks on every future stylesheet edit for no semantic reason and would not have caught either of those, because a reader that mangles nested selectors can still return the right number and one that drops nested rules can still return a different right number.

  `declarations(body, prop)` — one property's values from an already comment-stripped body, anchored on a declaration boundary (start of body, or after a ';') rather than a bare substring, with a trailing chunk after the last ';' treated as a declaration. THE REASONS FOR THE ANCHORING ARE MEASURED, NOT ELEGANT, and one common reason is false: 'min-width' is NOT a substring of 'min-height'. The reasons that are real, both green today: (a) a rule with no min-width at all but a comment naming one reads as ['16ch'], count 1, GREEN — the BUG-1 state passing the BUG-1 pin, because the min-width pin does not strip comments while the card pin beside it does; (b) a comment standing beside a real declaration is consumed as the declaration, so widths comes back ['0','16ch'] where the real floor is 16ch. The third thing the boundary buys is the custom-property case: a bare substring search matches `--min-width: 16ch` and a boundary-anchored one does not, in a stylesheet whose `:root` declares seventeen custom properties. The trailing-chunk clause is a STATED LOOSENING, not a repair: dropping the trailing semicolon from `.page-title`'s `line-height: 1.25` and from `#main > *`'s `min-width: 0` is RED today because both existing regexes require the ';'. Nothing is silently removed; the file shouts, and tests[] pins both directions.

  `conflictingOverrides(rules, pinned, selectors, prop)` — the card pin's override loop, lifted out of that test's body and corrected. The property is a fourth argument and the filter `declarations(other.body, prop).length > 0` runs inside, because the card pin's existing /overflow-wrap\s*:/ filter is what makes the comment above it true — a rule that cannot override the card classes does not turn the suite red. Take the property away and you get one of two failures: drop the filter and a narrow-viewport padding tweak on a pinned selector turns the suite red for a declaration that cannot change the property, re-breaking a tolerance #71 added on purpose; or hardcode overflow-wrap inside and the non-wrap pins get a check that can never fire. `pinned` is the rule or the SET of rules the calling pin has already asserted on, and every member is exempt — the new pin's collection is a set, and without the exemption the fix is reported as an override of itself. A conflict is reported for any rule other than the pinned set, at ANY source index, top-level or nested, declaring `prop` on a comma-split selector part equal to a member of `selectors`. Symmetric in source order, because an override authored above the pinned rule wins at narrow viewports exactly as one below does, and the shipped forced-colors carve-out is the one existing case of that shape.

  THE SELECTOR LOOKUP MUST ANCHOR ON THE SELECTOR'S END — compare a comma-split part to the pinned selector with `===`, never `selector.includes(pinnedSelector)`. '.opportunity-roww' and '.tenant-names' both contain their pinned selector as a substring; the current `\s*\{` anchors give the pins their rename protection today, and a substring lookup deletes it across all eight pins at once, invisibly.

  WHERE THE CONFLICT CHECK IS CALLED, and this is the design decision that matters most. Call it at the card pin (1691) and at the new .awaiting-list pin ONLY. 1652 (#main > *), 1663 (.table-scroll), 1756 (.approval-actions), 1766 (.approval-actions input), 1801 (.journal-drawer-body) and 1818 (.tenant-name) each already collect EVERY rule matching their selector and assert the property on every one of them, so their every-match loop IS the same coverage a same-selector conflict check would give — and because the helper exempts the pinned set, and the pinned set on those six is every rule that could ever match, the call can never fire there. It is dead code that reads as coverage. Put one line in each of those six tests' comments saying the every-match loop is that selector's override check, so the absence reads as a decision. Add one contract case distinguishing a pin whose pinned set is the whole selector from one whose pinned set is a single rule, so the distinction cannot rot silently.

  TWO PINS THAT ARE NOT MECHANICAL. `.page-title` (1632) asserts EVERY .page-title rule rather than the first: an appended `.page-title { margin: 4rem }` is green under a first-match check and the page breaks. `#main:focus` (344) needs an exact count, not a conflict check, because the conflict check is genuinely unavailable there: its one later same-selector rule IS the intentional forced-colors carve-out, so any same-selector override check reports it by design. The count pin — exactly one top-level #main:focus rule declaring `outline: none`, and exactly one not at top level carrying the carve-out — goes on THAT test of the two, stated here so the implementer does not have to choose.

  THE FORCED-COLORS PIN, the third place that needs care, and the loosening is accepted on purpose and pinned. The current regex at pages.test.js:360 is /@media\s*\(forced-colors:\s*active\)\s*\{[^@]*?#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/, and its `[^@]*?` means it only finds the carve-out when it is the first thing in the block. The reader finds it wherever it sits, so the rewrite is strictly MORE PERMISSIVE. The assertions that carry the meaning are unchanged — the carve-out exists, declares `outline: 2px solid CanvasText`, and comes after the bare #main:focus rule at equal specificity, both selectors being 1,1,0 — and a mutation that puts another nested rule before the carve-out must still pass, so the loosening is a stated behaviour. The test's comment says the parser's strictness changed, not the assertion. Keep the `length > 0` guard on the not-at-top-level lookup specifically, so a reader regression that stopped descending into at-rules cannot make this test pass vacuously on a file with no carve-out at all. The source-order assertion at pages.test.js:372-377 is the only thing in the suite that pins WHY the carve-out wins, and its comment says so; it must survive the rewrite as a comparison of the two rules' SOURCE INDICES rather than of character offsets, deliberately, not by accident.

  THE NEW .awaiting-list li PIN, in the house style of #main > * and .tenant-name rather than a whole-body assertion, and in ONE test. In order: (a) collect every rule that is NOT nested, whose comma-split selector part is `.awaiting-list` or `.awaiting-list li`, and whose body declares overflow-wrap — the property filter is part of the COLLECTION predicate, not only inside the helper, and the test's comment must say that in those terms, because the media-nested rule's selector part IS exactly '.awaiting-list li' and an unfiltered collection takes it in, at which point deepEqual([], ['anywhere']) fails and the suite goes red for a padding declaration; (b) require the collection NON-EMPTY, with a message that says so, so deleting the declaration and leaving a comment is red; (c) require each collected rule's overflow-wrap values to deepEqual ['anywhere']; (d) run `conflictingOverrides(rules, collected, ['.awaiting-list', '.awaiting-list li', '.awaiting-list li strong', '.awaiting-list li span'], 'overflow-wrap')` and require it to report nothing. Today the file yields exactly one `.awaiting-list li` rule with zero overflow-wrap declarations in it, so (b) is what turns the current state red rather than vacuous. Two strictnesses with their costs recorded in out_of_scope: `.awaiting-list` (the ul) is in the collection's selector set, because `overflow-wrap` is inherited and the pin must not report a correct fix on the parent as absent; and the collection requires the declaration at TOP LEVEL, because a fix authored only inside `@media (max-width: 900px)` satisfies the new pin in full AND satisfies the whole browser sweep at 320 / 375 / 414, all of which are inside that query, while the defect is not inherently narrow-viewport.

  (e) the render half, in the same test, AS A LINK ASSERTION AND NOTHING MORE. Use `seededRepos(prefix)` — which creates tenant_demo and the seeded decisions — NOT bare `freshRepos()`, which has no tenant, and `decisionsOf` at src/web/pages.js:614-619 is `if (!tenant) { return []; }`, so the page renders the empty branch with no `class="awaiting-list"` anywhere. Before rendering, assert that `repos.tenants.list()` is exactly one row and its id is `tenant_demo`, with a message saying the fixture's tenant selection is load-bearing for `firstTenant()` — that assertion is what stops a future seed adding a second tenant from repointing the whole page, and it is the same check that proves a seeded database was served. Then create ONE further decision on top of the seed through the NINE-FIELD `repos.decisions.create(...)` of R2, whose decision_id is 140 unbreakable characters, and assert that /journal at override 'partial' emits `class="awaiting-list"` and an `<li data-decision-id=...>` whose `<strong>` holds that id whole. The assertion is that the selector is a fact about the page and the id is not truncated in the data layer. It is NOT a measurement of layout and must not be described as one: the renderer reads no stylesheet — the shell links it at pages.js:68 and the asset route serves it at src/api/routes.js:263 — this repository has no browser driver, and this half passes with or without the declaration. The 140 characters are kept because they make the selector's purpose legible to the next reader, not because their length is doing work, and the test's comment must say so in those terms. The half does NOT assert 'and nothing else': .journal-drawer-body already carries overflow-wrap alongside four other declarations in one rule, and a whole-body assertion would force the fix into a second `.awaiting-list li` rule whose duplicate selector the conflict check reads as an override of itself.

  ONE CONTRACT TEST for the helpers, driven by fixture strings rather than the shipped stylesheet, covering the nine cases in tests[]. The eight-pin migration otherwise has no automated guard on its own plumbing — every proof it works is a mutation a reviewer runs by hand, and the helpers will outlive this ticket.

C. Repair the pre-existing red test, because nothing else in this change is verifiable while it is red. I RAN IT: 72 tests, 71 pass, 1 fail, and the failure is pages.test.js:1779 with the message 'a pending approval renders the card the pins above are about'. The critique returned 'flawed' with eight findings, two blocking. I reproduced all eight against this tree rather than taking them on trust, upheld the two blocking and two of the majors, folded in one more, and dismissed three — and I found two defects neither document saw. The disagreement is real in both directions and I am not presenting a consensus.

WHAT THE CRITIQUE CHANGED. Its first blocking finding is the best catch in the round and the proposal missed it entirely: the qa_script seeds one database and serves another, so every browser acceptance in the order measured an empty instance. I ran the boot string verbatim and got a 225280-byte ./data/app.db beside a 4096-byte served file, zero `awaiting-list` occurrences, and — the part that makes it worse than a typo — still zero after a valid snapshot and a valid decision both returned 201, because the API does not create a tenant row and `firstTenant()` returns null. A step that posts a decision and then asserts the page renders it is the natural repair, and it does not work; I tried it. That is now AC-12 and a boot assertion QA runs before any measurement. Its second blocking finding is equally real: the render half is specified as a two-field `repos.decisions.create(...)` that throws a node:sqlite bind TypeError, and the proposal's supporting claim that the repository 'does no validation' is what made it look fine. I ran it. Its second major finding is the same defect class the brief rejected v4 and v5 for — AC-8's `grep -n 'matchAll'` returning nothing, when four of the eighteen matches parse rendered HTML and one of those four is inside the card pin's own render half that AC-6 requires be kept — and I am not passing it through a fourth time. Its fourth major finding is right in substance: 'ch-only' appears in the proposal's understanding, tests, risks, assumptions and rationale and NOWHERE in files[], while files[] promises every assertion and message stays verbatim. I read the pin; the regex is (ch|rem|px) and the message says 'in ch, rem or px', so the narrowing necessarily edits both, and 12px and 96px are both green today exactly as claimed. Its third major finding is right about a real exposure — `firstTenant()` takes `tenants.list()[0]` — and I took its fix, because the assertion costs two lines and doubles as the check that a seeded database is the one being served.

WHAT I REJECTED, and the critic is wrong on each. Finding 5 asks the new pin to also watch `.panel strong`, on the ground that the plan treats a hypothetical `.panel strong` as an acceptable residual while treating a hypothetical second `min-width` value in a rule it is editing as blocking. But the plan does not merely accept that hole — it names it in residual_risks with the mechanism and the styles.css:195 precedent, and qa_script has a dedicated step that appends the exact form, confirms the overflow returns, and reverts it. That is a chosen hole with a probe pointed at it, not a missed one, and the proposed fix is worse: overflow-wrap can arrive on ANY descendant of the li, so a fifth selector makes the list look exhaustive without making it so, while making a correct unrelated rule red for a reason the ticket cannot state. I kept the recording and said in residual_risks that the asymmetry was chosen. Finding 6 objects that AC-9 hard-codes `12` in how_to_verify, and its own evidence confirms the arithmetic is right, the check itself is the single readFileSync(new URL count, and the 19 -> 12 pair is prose describing a transition rather than a second acceptance assertion. Finding 7 says the card pin's render loop should be named as the canary for the raw-event removal, and its own evidence calls the existing coverage 'adequate' and concedes tests[] already asserts the case. I named the canary line in files[] anyway because it costs nothing — not because the finding was right, and I do not want that recorded as a fix.

WHAT BOTH DOCUMENTS MISSED, which is where I think the round's real value was. tests[] contradicts itself on `min-width: 96px`: one case says the pin goes RED on it, another two cases later says it 'stays GREEN on 96px only because ch-only narrowing rejects it', which is incoherent. An implementer cannot satisfy both sentences, and both the proposal and the critique discuss the narrowing without noticing the contradiction inside it. Separately, AC-8 and AC-9 assert the same grep and the same number, so a reviewer sees one fact claimed twice and cannot tell whether it is two obligations. Both are now resolved: 96px goes red, and AC-8 owns the parser population while AC-9 owns the read count.

WHERE I DISAGREE WITH BOTH, which is the residue of two earlier rounds. The 96px mutation is listed in AC-5 beside the 12px one, and 12px is the sharp case because the reporter MEASURED it at clientWidth 59px — byte-identical to the BUG-1 state. 96px is 96 pixels; it is not narrow, and the only reason it goes red is that the regex refuses a unit it cannot compare. The proposal's risks entry is honest that this is a judgement; I have now made it an edit with a named cost rather than a criterion resting on a change no document asked for, which is the right place for it and the only reason I am willing to keep it at all. The second disagreement is about the diagnosis's own silence: nothing in this repository can observe the defect this ticket fixes, and the whole test half is about the parser instead. That is defensible — the layout defect was found in a browser, and a browser is where it must be re-checked — but it means the automated half of this order proves the pin works, not that the page is fixed. I have put that first in residual_risks rather than leaving it in out_of_scope where an earlier round put a false 'measured and safe' entry that caused all of this.
